- When sentiment is strongly negative (e.g., < -1.5) in recent days, model tends to overcorrect upward — reduce forecast peak by 5–10%.
- After a sharp price spike, model often overshoots and fails to correct — cap forecast decline after peak at 10–15% below peak.
- If sentiment swings sharply from positive to negative, model overreacts and forecasts too low — adjust downward only if sentiment confirms sustained bearish trend.
- Mean reversion bias: if 3–5 consecutive days show price moving away from 30-day moving average, model tends to overcorrect — reduce forecast by 2–5% for next 3–5 days.
- For 30-day forecasts, if sentiment is neutral or mildly positive, model often overestimates — reduce forecast by 3–7% if recent 7-day average sentiment > 0.5.
- If sentiment is consistently positive but price is flat or declining, model overestimates — reduce forecast by 5–10% if sentiment > 1.0 but price is below 30-day MA.
- Avoid forecasting sharp upward moves when sentiment is mixed or negative — cap forecast at 10% below recent 14-day high if sentiment < 0.5.
